units.latency: milliseconds per token (decode) or per 2048-token prefill
units.device_time: microseconds summed over the tt-perf-report signposted window

note: baseline = tt/fused_decoder.py, optimized = tt/optimized_decoder.py.  Latency rows come from probes/sweep.py (one process, real Qwen3.6-27B weights, 32 warmed traced decode replays, 3 warmed prefills); device rows come from the Tracy runs in tracy/. Decode is traced: capture once, then execute_trace replays inside the window.

workload.layers_measured: one per HF layer kind (layer 0 linear_attention, layer 3 full_attention)

model_scale.note: 64 layers: 48 linear_attention + 16 full_attention.  Layer stack only - no embedding, final norm, LM head or sampling, which the full-model stage owns.

named_limitations: paged decode SDPA keeps its softmax denominator in Float16_b: PCC falls from 0.99997 at position 63 to 0.78999 at 262143; inherited from the functional stage, see doc/context_contract.json and work_log.md section 10
every explicit SDPAProgramConfig is 4-9x faster and wrong at some positions, so none can be adopted (work_log.md section 10)
BFP4 decode matmuls reach ~299 GB/s against 442-477 GB/s for BFP8 at every geometry and in every matmul family (work_log.md section 3)

ttnn.transformer.gated_delta_attn_seq measured 0.9829 state PCC on the real layer's activations, unchanged when every Python-side precision knob is raised to HiFi4/fp32, so the loss is inside the C++ scan (work_log.md section 7)
a 2D matmul with a DRAM-width-sharded weight silently computes the wrong answer when out_block_w < per_core_N (work_log.md section 6)

the gated-delta-net causal conv carries 1.94 ms of tilize/untilize because a causal conv is a sum of row-shifted views; ttnn.conv1d refuses 10240 depthwise channels with an exact L1 blocker (work_log.md section 18)

BFP4 attention/gated-delta-net output projections and proj_fp32_acc=False are correct on real weights and 1.3% faster, but adopting them would need the synthetic-weight suite bar lowered from 0.98 to about 0.96 (work_log.md section 9)
